Mellin transformation gives the exact positive convolution kernel. Right translations prove the half-line essential norm equals the whole-line periodic norm. Floquet kernels are pointwise bounded by the positive zero-quasi-momentum kernel, whose Fourier matrix is the compact Jacobi operator. Explicit input/output boundary estimates certify finite truncations. Simple-eigenvalue analytic perturbation of D(I+epsilon X)^2D, with the two +/-1 neighboring states, yields the stated exact second-order coefficient and the unitary sign symmetry removes odd terms. Finite numpy tests checked supplementary numerical values, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Log-periodic output coefficients of generalized Hilbert matrices are a natural boundary case beyond converging local means and fixed-scale multiplicative slow oscillation. The theorem reduces an infinite-dimensional noncompact essential norm to a compact Jacobi norm, provides exponential finite-section certification for arbitrary positive frequency and real |epsilon|<1, and gives a sharp nontrivial frequency-dependent quadratic response. This directly quantifies interaction of Carleman spectral mixing and logarithmic scale oscillation rather than reporting a routine weight bound.
